items.title: Economic burden and quality of life of IgG4-related disease in China: A comparative analysis of three treatment regimens.
items.abstract: IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) is a chronic fibroinflammatory disorder requiring prolonged treatment, placing substantial financial burden on patients. This study compares the direct medical costs of three treatment regimens-glucocorticoid (GC), GC combined with Mycophenolate mofetil (MMF), and rituximab (RTX) -and evaluates the patients' health-related quality of life (HR-QoL) using the EuroQol 5-Dimension 5-Level scale (EQ-5D-5 L) to assess cost-effectiveness. Our retrospective cohort study consecutively distributed EQ-5D-5 L questionnaires to treatment-naïve IgG4-RD outpatients. Patients formed three cohorts: 30 with GC, 30 with GC+MMF, and 20 with RTX. Patients on other regimens were excluded. HR-QoL was assessed using EQ-5D-5 L questionnaires and visual analog scales. Quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) were calculated, and incremental cost-effectiveness ratios were computed. Probabilistic sensitivity analysis with Monte Carlo simulations evaluated cost-effectiveness across willingness-to-pay thresholds. First-year treatment costs were $1284.53 for GC, $2090.96 for GC+MMF, and $6175.97 for RTX. RTX group demonstrated the lowest relapse rate. No significant differences were observed in HR-QoL scores among groups, though visual analog scale (VAS) scores favored GC over GC+MMF. Median incremental cost-effectiveness ratios of probabilistic sensitivity analysis were $13,310/QALY for RTX versus GC and $17,412/QALY for RTX versus GC+MMF. GC demonstrated highest cost-effectiveness probability at willingness-to-pay thresholds below $15,000/QALY. Inverse probability of treatment weighting analysis confirmed these findings' robustness after controlling for selection bias. While RTX offers superior efficacy with lowest relapse rates, its high price leads to limited usage in China. GC-based regimens provide reasonable outcomes at lower costs, making GC or GC+MMF more economical choices.

items.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing highlights the heterogeneity of neutrophils in granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
items.abstract: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA), a clinical phenotype of anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis, is characterized by necrotizing inflammation of blood vessels. While neutrophil dysregulation is central to its pathogenesis, its cellular heterogeneity and dynamic functional states remain poorly defined. To better understand the transcriptomic profile of neutrophils, we applied single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to peripheral blood samples from GPA patients and healthy controls (HCs). Peripheral blood samples were collected from three patients with active GPA and three HCs, followed by sequencing using the BD Rhapsody platform (Becton, Dickinson and Company). In a subsequent validation cohort, flow cytometry and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction were used to confirm specific neutrophil subtypes and explore their potential clinical significance. Seven neutrophil clusters with distinct transcriptomic and functional profiles were identified. CXCL8-high and TXNIP-high subsets, predominant in HCs and GPA patients respectively, showed inflammatory profiles. CXCL8-high subsets also expressed immunoregulatory molecules to restrain inflammation. MMP8-high neutrophils showed enhanced antimicrobial activity, whereas IFIT1-high cells were linked to antiviral responses, suggesting that prior infections may contribute to anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV) pathogenesis. PLA2G7-high neutrophils, identified as terminally differentiated by pseudotime analysis, were associated with disease relapse and renal involvement, indicating potential as AAV biomarkers. Transcriptional profiles of peripheral T and natural killer (NK) cells were also characterized, along with the analysis of systemic immune cell-cell communication networks. Our study enhances the understanding of the dynamic functional roles of neutrophils in GPA and may facilitate the development of therapeutic strategies aimed at selectively targeting disease-specific neutrophil subsets.

items.title: Disease burden of rheumatoid arthritis in the context of population aging: A comparative analysis of China, Japan, the United States and India.
items.abstract: As worldwide population aging accelerates, the burden of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) continues to increase. This study compared the spatiotemporal trends and underlying drivers of the RA burden across four countries with different levels of socioeconomic development under population aging. Using data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 study, we analyzed age-standardized rates of incidence, prevalence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) for RA in China, Japan, the United States, and India from 1990 to 2021. Temporal trends were assessed using Joinpoint regression. A decomposition model was applied to quantify the contributions of population growth, population aging, and epidemiological changes to the overall burden. Spearman correlation analysis was performed to evaluate the association between RA burden indicators and the Sociodemographic Index (SDI). The Nordpred model was employed to project age-standardized prevalence rates among individuals aged 60 years and older up to 2046. From 1990 to 2021, the numbers of incident cases, prevalent cases, and DALYs attributable to RA increased substantially in China, the United States, and India ( e.g ., prevalent cases in China rose from 2.04 million to 4.76 million, and DALYs increased from 403,000 to 834,000), whereas the corresponding trends in Japan remained relatively stable. Age-standardized DALY rates increased significantly in China and India but exhibited a declining trend in Japan. Decomposition analysis revealed that the rise in RA burden in China was jointly driven by population aging and population growth, while in Japan, population aging alone accounted for nearly the entire increase. RA prevalence showed a strong positive correlation with SDI ( r = 0.82, P < 0.001). Projections indicate that by 2046, the age-standardized prevalence of RA among older adults will continue to rise in China, the United States, and India, whereas Japan is expected to reach a plateau. The burden of RA remains substantial in China, the United States, and India, and has shown a continuous upward trend, with older women being at particularly high risk. Population aging and population growth are the main driving factors. These findings highlight the need to establish a targeted comprehensive prevention and control system for RA among older adults and formulate differentiated, forward-looking health policies aligned with population aging trends to mitigate the future disease burden.

items.title: A Combinatorial mRNA Therapy for Treating Rheumatoid Arthritis and Osteoarthritis by Inhibiting Inflammation and Preventing Cartilage Degeneration.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and osteoarthritis (OA) are debilitating joint disorders with distinct etiologies but share common pathological features of chronic inflammation and progressive cartilage damage. Current therapeutic options are largely palliative and yet fail to achieve desired effect. In this study, we developed a combinatorial mRNA therapy using a rationally engineered lipid nanoparticle (LNP) containing a novel ionizable lipid for enhanced cartilage penetration upon intra-articular administration. This LNP co-delivers mRNAs encoding two complementary therapeutic proteins: interleukin-1 receptor antagonist (IL-1Ra) for inflammation attenuation and a C-terminal truncated derivative of angiopoietin-like 3 (ANL3) for cartilage degeneration prevention. In pre-clinical models including collagen-induced arthritis mice, TNF-transgenic mice with spontaneous RA and destabilization of medial meniscus (DMM) surgical OA model, this dual therapy significantly ameliorated disease severity, reduced synovitis and bone erosion, and potently repaired cartilage damage. Mechanistically, transcriptomic profiling of joint specimens revealed that the combinatorial therapy concurrently suppressed inflammatory pathways and extracellular matrix degradation pathways, meanwhile upregulating anabolic genes facilitating chondrogenesis. Collectively, our study establishes a versatile and synergistic mRNA therapy that offers a potent disease-modifying immunomodulatory strategy capable of addressing the long-standing unmet needs in arthritis treatment.

items.title: Colchicine usage and recurrent pericarditis in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: ObjectivePericarditis is a common and recurring manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). While guidelines for the management of SLE include the use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), colchicine, and glucocorticoids, the evidence for various treatments in SLE is limited. Evidence for the usage of colchicine for pericarditis in patients with SLE exists primarily in case reports and case series. The purpose of this study was to investigate colchicine usage and rates of recurrent pericarditis among patients with SLE.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included patients with SLE treated at a tertiary care center between 2015 and 2025. Patients were included if they presented to the hospital with pericarditis based on the 2025 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) Guidelines and had follow-up for at least 1 year. Based on the ESC guidelines, recurrent pericarditis was defined as new symptoms or disease activity after clinical remission and was captured within 1 year of the initial presentation.ResultsOf the 55 patients included in the study, 47.3% received colchicine, 52.7% received NSAIDs and 56.4% received glucocorticoids. Recurrent pericarditis occurred in 45.5% of patients. In univariate analyses, age less than 40 years at first presentation of pericarditis was significantly associated with recurrent pericarditis as was treatment with an initiation or increase of glucocorticoids. Treatment with colchicine trended toward reduced recurrence, but the result was not statistically significant. In multivariate logistic regression including age, treatment with colchicine, and treatment with glucocorticoids, only treatment with glucocorticoids was significantly associated with recurrent pericarditis (odds ratio 4.31; 95% confidence interval 1.12-16.55).ConclusionsIn this study, recurrent pericarditis was common among patients with SLE and was associated with treatment with glucocorticoids. Colchicine was associated with a trend toward decreased recurrence rates, but this was not statistically significant. Given high recurrence rates among patients treated with steroids, additional studies are needed on non-steroidal therapies for pericarditis in SLE, including further research on colchicine.

items.title: Ten-Year Longitudinal Changes in Nailfold Videocapillaroscopy Findings and Clinical Features in Systemic Sclerosis.
items.abstract: To investigate whether 10-year changes in nailfold videocapillaroscopy (NVC) findings are associated with changes in clinical characteristics in systemic sclerosis (SSc). This retrospective single-center study included 84 patients with SSc who underwent NVC assessment at baseline and after 10 years. NVC patterns were classified as normal, non-specific, early, active, or late. Patients were categorized by longitudinal NVC changes. Associations of NVC-change groups with changes in clinical characteristics including modified Rodnan skin score (mRSS), digital ulcers, interstitial lung disease, percent predicted vital capacity (%VC), and percent predicted diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (%DLco) were examined. Over 10 years, NVC findings improved in 19 patients, remained unchanged in 41, and worsened in 24. Change in mRSS differed significantly among the groups, with greater improvement in the improved group than in the unchanged group (p = 0.0140) and the worsened group (p = 0.0161). Changes in digital ulcers were not associated with NVC-change groups. Among 47 patients with longitudinal %DLco data, Δ%DLco differed significantly among the groups, with the greatest decline in the worsened group (p = 0.0067), whereas Δ%VC did not differ significantly. NVC-change group was significantly associated with mRSS at 10 years after adjustment for baseline mRSS and disease duration (p = 0.0291), but not with Δ%DLco after adjustment for interstitial lung disease and pulmonary hypertension at 10 years (p = 0.0684). In conclusion, long-term NVC changes may occur in both directions may reflect the long-term course of skin sclerosis.

items.title: Spatiotemporally Precise Rheumatoid Arthritis Therapy via a Triple-Locked Cascaded Nanoplatform With Dual-Channel Self-Reporting.
items.abstract: Achieving precise spatiotemporal control over combination therapies in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) remains heavily compromised by conventional nanoplatforms, which typically suffer from premature off-target leakage, coupled drug release, and inadequate in vivo tracking capabilities. Herein, a programmable orthogonally branched triple-locked nanotheranostic platform (MB@YW NPs) is engineered to seamlessly synchronize spatial localization, chemically orthogonal multidrug liberation, and real-time multichannel self-reporting. The system comprises a pH-responsive polymeric matrix co-encapsulating a HOCl-activatable methotrexate prodrug (MB-MTX) and an ONOO - /light-responsive sulfasalazine prodrug (YW-SSZ). Precluding systemic leakage, synovial acidity dictates initial spatial targeting by triggering tissue-specific disassembly and subsequent macrophage internalization. Subsequently, non-interfering pathophysiological triggers exclusively liberate distinct therapeutics through independent pathways: intracellular HOCl purely unlocks methotrexate with concomitant near-infrared "turn-on" fluorescence, whereas an isolated ONOO - /light sequence locally activates sulfasalazine accompanied by a blue "on-to-off" readout. This lack of cross-talk successfully discriminates multiplexed activation states. In vivo, this triple-locked platform efficiently alleviates oxidative stress and remodels the inflammatory microenvironment, leading to markedly suppressed joint destruction in collagen-induced arthritis models. Furthermore, transcriptomic analysis reveals these synergistic macroscopic benefits are driven by targeted modulation of the cAMP/NF-κB signaling axis. Collectively, this work establishes a transformative and generalizable framework for independently coordinated, next-generation precision multi-prodrug nanomedicine.

items.title: Juvenile dermatomyositis across diagnostic eras: treatment evolution and long-term outcomes in a 25-year cohort.
items.abstract: Juvenile dermatomyositis (JDM) is a rare autoimmune myopathy with heterogeneous phenotypes and variable long-term outcomes. We aimed to summarize a 25-year single-center cohort and to evaluate clinical characteristics, investigations, autoantibody profiles, treatments and determinants of cumulative damage. We retrospectively included 104 patients fulfilling the 2017 EULAR/ACR criteria (2000-2025) with ≥6 months follow-up. Clinical features, complications, investigations (EMG, MRI, biopsy), treatments and myositis-specific/associated antibodies were recorded. Diagnostic eras were defined as 2000-2007, 2008-2014 and 2015-2025. Damage was assessed using standardized and normalized MDI extent/extended scores and MyoDAM severity. The cohort showed female predominance (66.3%). Mean age at onset and diagnosis were 7.7 ± 4.1 and 8.5 ± 4.2 years; median follow-up was 52.6 months. Skin involvement (91.3%) and proximal muscle weakness (79.8%) were the most frequent presenting features. Autoantibody frequencies were comparable to previous reports, although phenotype associations differed. Calcinosis increased from 13.5% at diagnosis to 40.4% overall; skin ulceration from 3.8% to 12.5%. Nailfold capillaroscopy abnormalities (57.5%) were associated with calcinosis (p = 0.031). Calcinosis frequency did not differ across eras (p = 0.535), and time-to-calcinosis curves were similar (log-rank p = 0.235). In multivariable analyses, diagnostic delay ≥6 months, chronic active course, dysphagia and cutaneous ulceration were independently associated with higher damage (adjusted R²: 0.416 for MDI extent; 0.403 for MDI extended; 0.449 for MyoDAM severity). Cumulative damage was primarily driven by delayed diagnosis, persistent disease course and severe vasculopathic/systemic features, underscoring the importance of early recognition and treat-to-target escalation to prevent long-term damage.

items.title: Lightweight interpretable support vector machine SERS (LiSVM-SERS) learning framework for serological diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis and biomarker identification.
items.abstract: Psoriatic arthritis (PsA), a chronic, autoimmune form of arthritis that causes joint inflammation and occurs with the skin condition psoriasis, is difficult to clinically diagnose at an early stage due to insignificant symptoms and lack of biomarkers. Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) is a powerful tool to identify specific biomolecules for liquid biopsy. Here, we establish a lightweight interpretable support vector machine SERS (LiSVM-SERS) learning framework for serological diagnosis of PsA and identification of potential biomarkers. The fs-laser-nanofabricated Au@mica SERS substrates with a relative standard deviation of 8.80% in intensity homogeneity are employed to obtain reliable serum Raman spectra. The SVM algorithm is performed to train the machine-learning model for PsA classification using only 26 samples (PsA = 13 and healthy controls = 13). The hyperplane coefficient vectors from the trained SVM model are then employed as the filtered weights of Raman shifts, followed by logistic-probability mapping and Welch's t-test to filter highly-significant spectral features, identifying 432 most-significant Raman shifts for 7 potential biomarkers. The trained LiSVM-SERS model demonstrates the outstanding sensitivity and specificity of 98.0% and 96.0%, respectively, validated by an internal independent blind-test cohort (PsA = 30, healthy controls = 30) and a cross disease-control cohort (systemic lupus erythematosus = 15, rheumatoid arthritis = 15, and osteoarthritis = 15). The present work not only provides a simple and lightweight non-invasive technique to diagnose PsA, but also paves a new way to identify the potential biomarkers from the label-free serum SERS spectra for autoimmune disorders.

items.title: Crystal Sensing and Neurogenic Inflammation in Gout: A Proposed Sensory Neuroimmune Framework for Flare Pain.
items.abstract: Gout is a crystal-induced inflammatory arthritis caused by deposition of monosodium urate (MSU) crystals. The established mechanistic model centers on innate immune recognition of MSU crystals, NLRP3 inflammasome activation, caspase-1-dependent interleukin-1β (IL-1β) maturation and neutrophil-rich synovitis. Although this framework remains fundamental, it does not fully account for the intensity of flare pain or its close coupling with vascular and inflammatory responses, while the mechanisms underlying flare recurrence remain incompletely understood. Increasing evidence indicates that nociceptive sensory neurons can actively regulate local inflammation rather than merely transmit pain. This article is a mechanistic narrative review and does not follow PRISMA-based systematic-review methodology. Relevant evidence was identified through structured searches of MEDLINE via PubMed and the Web of Science Core Collection, supplemented by backward and forward citation tracking. Current gout-specific experimental evidence supports two complementary mechanistic segments: TRPV4-dependent macrophage crystal sensing linked to NLRP3-IL-1β activation, and CXCL5-neuronal CXCR2-TRPA1 signaling linking inflammatory cues to nociceptor activation and vascular amplification. However, direct human evidence remains limited and compartment-specific, and a continuous macrophage-nociceptor-vascular-neutrophil circuit has not been demonstrated within the human gout joint. We therefore propose this sensory neuroimmune framework as a testable, evidence-integrating model rather than a fully validated linear pathway. Local neuroimmune priming, persistent sensory sensitization and possible dissociation between inflammatory and sensory resolution remain testable hypotheses requiring longitudinal human validation. This framework extends rather than replaces the MSU-NLRP3-IL-1β paradigm and identifies priorities for future mechanistic and translational investigation.

items.title: Successful extravascular implantable cardioverter defibrillator implantation in a patient with ankylosing spondylitis and severe thoracic deformity: a case report.
items.abstract: Severe thoracic deformity in ankylosing spondylitis (AS) can complicate implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) implantation and device selection. Substernal EV-ICD implantation requires careful anatomical assessment and individualized procedural planning. A 57-year-old male with severe AS and dilated cardiomyopathy was referred for primary prevention ICD implantation. Given the high complication risks associated with conventional approaches, EV-ICD was selected. A tailored positioning strategy was employed to accommodate the thoracic deformity. Intraoperative resistance during substernal dissection was successfully overcome through meticulous re-dissection. Favourable intraoperative electrical parameters were obtained, including an R-wave sensing amplitude of 5.6 mV without P-wave oversensing and successful defibrillation at 30 J on the first attempt. At 6-month follow-up, device performance remained stable without sensing anomalies or inappropriate shocks. This case demonstrates the technical feasibility of EV-ICD implantation in a carefully selected patient with severe AS-associated thoracic deformity. Preoperative CT assessment, tailored patient positioning, careful dissection, and surgical backup enabled successful implantation and stable device performance during 6 months of follow-up.

items.title: Incidence and characteristics of cytokine release syndrome in patients with systemic sclerosis undergoing autologous haematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a debilitating autoimmune connective tissue disease associated with high morbidity and mortality. Autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) improves survival in diffuse cutaneous SSc. Cytokine release syndrome (CRS), a potentially fatal inflammatory response, is a complication of HSCT associated with anti-thymocyte globulin use. This study aimed to systematically describe the incidence and characteristics of ATG-related CRS in SSc patients undergoing HSCT. SSc patients undergoing autologous HSCT according to the (adjusted) ASTIS protocol (2011-2025) were analysed retrospectively. CRS was graded according to American Society for Transplantation and Cellular Therapy (ASTCT) criteria. Associations between CRS ≥2 and clinical characteristics were explored, and overall survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Of the 91 eligible for grading, 81 (89.0%) were classified as having CRS: 40 (44.0%) as grade 1 (fever only), 26 (28.6%) as grade 2, ten (11.0%) as grade 3, three (3.3%) as grade 4, and two (2.2%) as grade 5 (fatal). Among the 41 patients with grade ≥2 CRS, grading was based solely on respiratory criteria in 61.0%. No significant associations with grade ≥2 CRS remained after multiple-testing correction. Overall survival did not differ significantly, although the Kaplan-Meier curves separated early. Follow-up lung function and skin scores were similar between groups. CRS is highly prevalent and clinically relevant in SSc patients undergoing autologous HSCT. The frequent respiratory manifestations may reflect SSc-related pre-existing cardiopulmonary involvement, vasculopathy, and fluid exposure during conditioning, rather than inflammation alone, suggesting a distinct CRS phenotype.

items.title: IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-10, IL-17 and IL-22 secretion capacities and activation profile of T cells in psoriatic arthritis patients under disease-modifying antirheumatic drug therapy.
items.abstract: While biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (bDMARDs) have transformed management, achieving complete remission remains a challenge due to complex immune networks in Psoriatic arthritis (PsA). This study aimed to characterize the functional modulation of circulating T-helper (Th) and cytotoxic T (Tc) cells in PsA patients following conventional synthetic (csDMARD) and biologic therapy. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were collected from bDMARD-naïve PsA patients at baseline and six months after initiating csDMARD (primarily methotrexate, n=8) or bDMARD (primarily certolizumab, n=11) therapy. Using an optimized flow cytometry-based assay, we evaluated the secretion capacities of TNF-α, IFN-γ, IL-17, IL-22, and IL-10, alongside activation markers (CD40L, ICOS, CD38) in CD4 + Th and CD8 + Tc cells. Results were associated with clinical disease activity indices (DAPSA, BASDAI, PsAID-12, LEI). Both therapies significantly improved clinical scores yet failed to achieve immunological quiescence. A central finding was a significant increase in the percentage of TNF-secreting Th and Tc cells post-therapy, which may reflect a compensatory change in T-cell cytokine secretion following treatment. In the bDMARD cohort, Tc cells exhibited a significant expansion of subsets secreting IFN-γ, IL-17, and IL-10, suggesting a possible shift toward Type 1/Type 17-related cytokine responses. Baseline IL-17 and IL-10 levels correlated positively with high disease activity (BASDAI/PsAID-12), while post-treatment IL-17 and IL-22 secretory potential was specifically associated with persistent enthesitis (LEI scores). Despite clinical efficacy, DMARD therapy was associated with persistent alterations in T-cell cytokine profiles, including IFN-γ- and IL-17-producing T-cell populations, particularly within the CD8+ compartment. These findings suggest that peripheral immune profiling may provide additional insights into the immunological effects of therapy and could contribute to future personalized approaches for monitoring immune responses in patients with PsA.

items.title: Parenchymal Neuro-Behçet disease with heterogeneous clinical presentations: a comparative case report.
items.abstract: Neuro-Behçet disease (NBD) is a rare but potentially disabling manifestation of Behçet disease (BD). Its heterogeneous neurological presentation can mimic central nervous system infection, cerebrovascular disease, inflammatory demyelination or intracranial tumors, making early diagnosis difficult. Importantly, there is still limited published data on NBD from Palestine regarding presentation, diagnosis, imaging and management. We describe two patients with a long history of recurrent oral and genital ulceration who were diagnosed with parenchymal Neuro-Behçet disease (P-NBD). The first patient was a 26-year-old man with a two-week progressive headache, fever, vomiting, and blurred vision, which resembled meningitis, in whom examination showed central facial weakness, gait imbalance and pathological laughter. The second patient was a 41-year-old woman with a two-year history of gait imbalance and dysarthria who presented with three days of dizziness, horizontal nystagmus, central facial weakness, right lower-limb weakness, and a positive bilateral extensor plantar response. Laboratory testing and brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) were performed to exclude other differential diagnoses. Both received intravenous methylprednisolone followed by an immunosuppressive agent. The first patient had clinical and radiological improvement after corticosteroids and initiation of induction cyclophosphamide, with clinical improvement on follow-up. The second patient improved significantly on imaging after infliximab maintenance therapy. She also improved clinically, but chronic symptoms of gait imbalance and dysarthria were still present. These two cases illustrate the variable presentation of P-NBD, including a meningitis-like febrile syndrome with pathological laughter and an acute-on-chronic brainstem syndrome. In patients with recurrent oro-genital ulceration and unexplained brainstem or diencephalic neurological findings, NBD should be considered after careful exclusion of other disorders. Early diagnosis and immunosuppressive treatment can lead to substantial clinical and radiological improvement.

items.title: Candidate molecular endotypes and dynamic risk prediction in anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis-associated interstitial lung disease: a systematic scoping review.
items.abstract: Anti-melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 antibody-positive dermatomyositis (anti-MDA5+ DM) spans pulmonary states from no detectable interstitial lung disease (ILD) to rapidly progressive ILD (RP-ILD). We mapped molecular programs and prediction evidence to determine how recurrent biological states may support dynamic stratification. PubMed, Web of Science, Ovid and Embase were searched from inception to 22 August 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data. Reporting followed PRISMA-ScR; evidence was synthesized across molecular and prediction domains. Of 4, 166 records, 2, 317 remained after deduplication, 349 underwent full-text assessment, and 95 sources (80 primary studies and 15 syntheses) were included. Type I/III interferon signaling was the most reproducible program. Myeloid inflammatory-remodeling, adaptive activation with lymphocyte or natural-killer-cell loss, vascular-coagulation injury, and immunometabolic disturbance formed additional overlapping axes aligned with pulmonary-state transitions. Clinical and radiomic models showed strong short-term discrimination; harmonized landmarks, calibration, geographic validation, and decision-timed molecular sampling would strengthen clinical use. The evidence supports an integrated map linking recurrent molecular programs to dynamic pulmonary risk. A calibrated clinical-imaging backbone, augmented by parsimonious molecular modules with incremental value and updated at prespecified landmarks, offers a practical framework for prospective endotype validation and treatment-aware prediction in anti-MDA5+ DM-ILD. https://doi.org/10.37766/inplasy2026.10.0018, identifier INPLASY2026100018.

items.title: Exercise, physical activity, and physical fitness in psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis: an umbrella review.
items.abstract: Exercise, physical activity, and physical fitness are increasingly discussed in psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis (PsA), but the evidence base is uneven: intervention reviews predominantly concern PsA, whereas evidence for cutaneous psoriasis is largely observational or embedded in broader lifestyle interventions. This systematic review was conducted as an umbrella review of intervention effects and observational exposure-outcome associations. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261403713). PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus, and SPORTDiscus were searched from inception to 1 March 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data, with disagreements resolved by discussion and, when necessary, a third reviewer. Reporting followed PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 and PRIOR (Preferred Reporting Items for Overviews of Reviews). AMSTAR 2 (A Measurement Tool to Assess Systematic Reviews 2), corrected covered area (CCA), GRADE (Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluations), and the Ioannidis credibility classification were applied as appropriate. Nine reviews were included. Eight reviews provided PsA evidence, including interventional, descriptive, or observational findings; one observational meta-analysis concerned prevalent cutaneous psoriasis. No eligible review isolated the effect of exercise on cutaneous-psoriasis severity. Overall confidence was Moderate for one review, Low for five, and Critically Low for three. No umbrella-level pooling was undertaken because the same trials recurred across reviews, particularly in the high-intensity interval-training/cardiorespiratory cluster (CCA approximately 16.7%), and populations, outcomes, comparators, and effect measures were heterogeneous. Vigorous activity (RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.67 to 0.85) and regular exercise frequency (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.82 to 0.95) were associated with lower psoriasis prevalence, both with suggestive credibility. In PsA, possible improvements in fitness, disease activity, pain, function, and body composition were based mainly on single small trials and had very low certainty. The evidence differs by disease. For cutaneous psoriasis, current findings are observational and do not establish an exercise effect on disease severity or incidence. For PsA, intervention findings are sparse, duplicated across reviews, and of very low certainty. Safety reporting was incomplete and did not permit a disease-specific conclusion. Adequately powered, prospectively registered trials with disease-specific outcomes and systematic adverse-event reporting are required. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261403713.

items.title: Prognostic factors for long-term survival in anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis: a 10-year cohort study.
items.abstract: Anti-melanoma differentiation-associated gene 5-positive dermatomyositis (anti-MDA5+ DM) is a severe subtype frequently complicated by rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease (RP-ILD), leading to high early mortality. However, factors associated with long-term survival beyond 10 years remain largely uncharacterized. This exploratory analysis aimed to identify baseline factors associated with long-term all-cause mortality in a 10-year follow-up cohort using LASSO-Cox regression. This retrospective longitudinal study enrolled 84 inpatients diagnosed with anti-MDA5+ DM between 2010 and June 2014; surviving patients had more than 10 years of potential follow-up until March 2026. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. All candidate covariates, including clinical features, laboratory parameters, HRCT score, and initial treatment variables, were entered simultaneously into LASSO-penalized Cox regression with 10-fold cross-validation, and retained variables were directly entered into a multivariable Cox model. The proportional hazards assumption was tested, and bootstrap resampling was performed to assess selection stability. Survival was illustrated using Kaplan-Meier curves with log-rank tests. Among the 84 patients (27 males and 57 females), 41 (48.8%) were alive at the final follow-up and 43 (51.2%) had died. As a descriptive observation, 25 surviving patients (29.8% of the total cohort) had maintained sustained drug-free remission for over 2 years. Four baseline factors were independently associated with long-term mortality. Older age (HR = 1.05 per 1-year increase, P  < 0.001), fever on admission (HR = 2.08, P  = 0.036), and higher HRCT score (HR = 1.94 per 1-point increase, P  < 0.001) were associated with higher mortality, whereas concurrent arthritis was associated with lower mortality (HR = 0.45, P  = 0.022). Male sex showed a trend toward higher mortality that was not statistically significant after adjustment ( P  = 0.086). Older age, admission fever, higher HRCT score, and absence of arthritis - all assessable at admission - were independently associated with all-cause mortality over long-term follow-up in the full anti-MDA5+ DM cohort; landmark analysis showed only arthritis and HRCT score remained associated with mortality after year 1. Given the limited sample size and lack of external validation, these exploratory findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in independent multicenter cohorts.

items.title: Epstein-Barr virus shapes intrathecal Th1/Th17 immunity and parenchymal involvement in neuro-Behçet's disease.
items.abstract: Human herpesviruses (HHVs) are implicated in neuro-inflammatory diseases due to their ability to establish persistent latency and reactivate in the context of immune dysregulation. Whilst Epstein -Barr virus (EBV) is recognized as a key factor in multiple sclerosis (MS), its role in neuro-Behçet's disease (NBD) remains poorly understood. Serum and paired CSF samples were obtained from treatment-naïve patients with NBD and MS. Neurotropic viral DNA in CSF was screened by multiplex PCR. Virus-specific IgG antibodies against HSV-1 and EBV antigens (VCA and EBNA1) were measured by ELISA in serum and CSF. Real-time PCR was used to assess the expression of EBV latent genes (LMP1 and EBNA1), as well as cytokines and transcription factors, in CSF samples from NBD patients. In this study, we demonstrate a high prevalence of EBV DNA in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of patients with NBD (71.43%), significantly higher than that observed in MS (35.29%), whereas other neurotropic herpesviruses are rarely detected. Notably, the presence of EBV in the CSF is not associated with a specific intrathecal humoral response, suggesting predominantly latent viral persistence and cell-mediated immune control. The concurrent expression of the latent proteins LMP1 and EBNA1 indicates a type II latency program, capable of activating interferon pathways. EBV-positive patients exhibit an immune signature characterized by significantly elevated levels of IFN-γ and IFN-α, associated with Th1/Th17 polarization and reduced FOXP3 expression, reflecting a Th17/Treg imbalance. Furthermore, EBV status is associated with distinct clinical phenotypes, with parenchymal forms being observed exclusively in EBV-positive patients. This suggests that EBV may contribute to the pathophysiology of NBD by promoting a pro-inflammatory intrathecal microenvironment. It also positions EBV as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target in this condition.

items.title: Tripterygium wilfordii ameliorates complete freund adjuvant-induced rheumatoid arthritis through modulating the gut-joint axis.
items.abstract: Although Tripterygium wilfordii (TW) is a classical Chinese herbal medicine for the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), the mechanism by which it alleviates inflammation through modulation of the gut microbiota remains unclear. To elucidate the mechanism underlying the therapeutic effects of TW on RA, we first employed network pharmacology to predict the relevant pathways and core targets. Subsequently, an integrative multi-omics approach was applied, including gut metagenomics, gut metabolomics, serum metabolomics, and synovial transcriptomics, to investigate the alterations in gut microbiota, intestinal and serum metabolites, and synovial gene expression in a rat model of RA. Our findings revealed that TW supplementation lowered serum concentrations of IL-6, IL-1β, TNF-α, and IL-10 and modulated the Th17/Treg balance in intestinal tissue. TW treatment altered gut microbiota (GM) composition, marked by increased abundance of Prevotella sp PCJ2 and Psychrobacter pasteurii , and decreased Adlercreutzia equolifaciens and Schaedlerella arabinosiphila , synergizing with keystone species ( Bifidobacterium animalis, Phocaeicola sartorii, Blautia faecis ) to promote gut health. Concurrently, TW elevated tryptophan metabolites (tryptophol, tryptamine, 5-hydroxykynurenamine) while reducing 4-(2-aminophenyl)-2,4-dioxobutanoic acid, restoring tryptophan metabolism. This regulation coincided with upregulated Inmt mRNA in synovium, activating the tryptophan pathway. Correlation and mediation analyses indicated that gut-derived circulating metabolites such as N-myristoyl arginine and lauramidoxide were positively correlated with synovial Jun expression, potentially participating in the modulation of the IL-17-NF-κB cascade. Consistently, upregulated synovial Socs3 may exert negative feedback suppression on JAK-STAT signaling to alleviate inflammatory responses. These findings point to the gut microbiome and tryptophan pathway as a new therapeutic avenue for RA.

items.title: Late-onset versus young-onset rheumatoid arthritis: comorbidities, disease activity, and treatment patterns in a nationwide real-world registry from Kuwait.
items.abstract: Late-onset rheumatoid arthritis (LORA) may differ clinically from young-onset rheumatoid arthritis (YORA), but real-world data from the Middle East and North Africa are limited. We compared characteristics, comorbidities, disease activity, and treatment patterns between LORA and YORA in the Kuwait Registry for Rheumatic Diseases (KRRD) and assessed whether age at onset was independently associated with disease activity. This retrospective analysis of prospectively collected KRRD data included patients with RA enrolled between January 2012 and April 2026. Patients were classified as YORA (symptom onset 18-59 years) or LORA (≥60 years). Baseline characteristics, disease activity, treatments, and one-year outcomes were compared. Multivariable logistic regression examined factors associated with moderate-to-high disease activity (DAS28-ESR ≥3.2). Sensitivity analyses additionally adjusted for current age, assessed collinearity, and repeated comorbidity and ESR comparisons after age adjustment and within patients aged 60-79 years. Among 2,629 patients, 303 (11.5%) had LORA and 2,326 (88.5%) had YORA. LORA patients had shorter disease duration (2.9 ± 4.0 vs. 5.0 ± 7.1 years; p  < 0.001) and higher comorbidity burden (2.0 ± 1.5 vs. 0.9 ± 1.2; p  < 0.001). Most disease activity measures and treatment patterns were similar. Among 1,402 patients with follow-up of at least one year, disease activity at the last visit was similar (DAS28-ESR mean difference 0.10, 95% CI -0.12 to 0.30), including after inverse-probability weighting and multiple imputation. ESR was higher in LORA (40.9 vs. 33.3 mm/hr; p  < 0.001), whereas CDAI was not (mean difference 0.7, 95% CI -0.9 to 2.3). Age at onset was not independently associated with moderate-to-high disease activity (adjusted OR 1.08, 95% CI 0.83-1.41; p  = 0.559). After adjustment for current age and sex, the comorbidity excess in LORA was no longer evident (adjusted rate ratio 0.79, 95% CI 0.70-0.89), while ESR remained modestly higher (adjusted ratio 1.17, 95% CI 1.02-1.33). Adding current age did not materially change the onset-group estimate (adjusted OR 1.05, 95% CI 0.76-1.44). LORA and YORA showed similar disease activity, treatment patterns, and follow-up outcomes. The higher comorbidity burden in LORA was explained by chronological age, while ESR remained modestly elevated after age adjustment. Findings support treat-to-target principles regardless of age at onset, alongside management of comorbidities in older patients.

items.title: Empyema Due to Listeria monocytogenes in a Patient With Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Listeria monocytogenes is an uncommon cause of pleural empyema, particularly in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Disease and treatment-related immunosuppression increases susceptibility to invasive listeriosis, which carries significant mortality. A 78-year-old man with seropositive RA treated with methotrexate and low-dose corticosteroids presented with fever, hypotension, pleuritic chest pain, and weakness. Laboratory tests showed leukocytosis, neutrophilia, and elevated C-reactive protein. Imaging revealed a left pleural effusion with lower-lobe collapse. Thoracentesis drained 800 mL of exudative fluid, and cultures of pleural fluid and blood isolated L. monocytogenes . Cranial CT and lumbar puncture performed due to neurological symptoms were normal. High-dose ampicillin plus cotrimoxazole was administered for 7 days, followed by ampicillin monotherapy to complete a total of 14 days of antibiotic treatment, achieving progressive clinical and radiological improvement. Empyema caused by L. monocytogenes is rare and occurs mainly in immunocompromised hosts, with only isolated cases described in RA. This case underscores the need to consider Listeria infection in immunosuppressed RA patients presenting with pleural empyema. Listeria monocytogenes es una causa infrecuente de empiema pleural, especialmente en pacientes con artritis reumatoide (AR). La inmunosupresión relacionada con la enfermedad y su tratamiento aumenta la susceptibilidad a listeriosis invasiva, con significativa mortalidad. Un varón de 78 años con AR seropositiva tratado con metotrexato y corticoides a bajas dosis presentó fiebre, hipotensión, dolor torácico pleurítico y debilidad. La analítica mostró leucocitosis, neutrofilia y proteína C reactiva elevada. La imagen reveló un derrame pleural izquierdo con colapso del lóbulo inferior. La toracocentesis drenó 800 mL de líquido turbio exudativo, y los cultivos de líquido pleural y sangre aislaron Listeria monocytogenes . La tomografía craneal y la punción lumbar realizadas por síntomas neurológicos fueron normales. Se administró ampicilina a dosis altas asociada a cotrimoxazol durante 7 días, seguida de ampicilina en monoterapia hasta completar un total de 14 días de tratamiento antibiótico, con mejoría clínica y radiológica. El empiema por L. monocytogenes es excepcional y aparece sobre todo en pacientes inmunodeprimidos. Este caso destaca la necesidad de considerar Listeria en pacientes con AR inmunosuprimidos con empiema pleural.

items.title: A dual-track strategy: multi-target, bidirectional modulation of uric acid biosynthesis and renal elimination by natural products-molecular insights.
items.abstract: Hyperuricemia (HUA) arises primarily from increased urate production and an imbalance in extra-renal and renal urate excretion, and is accompanied by oxidative stress, inflammatory activation, and tissue injury. Such a networked pathophysiology constrains the utility of single-target intervention strategies. While currently used single-target urate-lowering agents can effectively reduce serum urate, limitations remain in indication selection, combination therapy, safety, and long-term adherence. Natural bioactive small molecules, characterized by multi-target actions and bidirectional regulation, have emerged as a valuable avenue for the integrated prevention and management of HUA and gout. This review summarizes urate-lowering natural products across multiple structural classes-including triterpenoids, flavonoids, phenolic acids, alkaloids, polyphenols, and anthraquinones-outlining their principal pharmacological mechanisms. In line with an 'efficacy-developability co-optimization' concept, we further discuss strategies for subsequent lead optimization of natural-product-derived scaffolds, aiming to support the discovery of novel urate-lowering leads and the development of multi-target anti-gout agents.

items.title: Anakinra for the Treatment of Severe Still's Disease Complicated With Macrophage Activation Syndrome.
items.abstract: To investigate the efficacy and safety of add-on anakinra for severe Still's disease complicated by macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) in a real-world setting. Consecutive patients aged ≥ 16 years with Still's disease and MAS (HLH-2004 criteria adapted for rheumatic diseases) who received anakinra 100 mg subcutaneously once daily were enrolled. Outcomes were CID, remission, and four EULAR/PReS-aligned targets, assessed at baseline, Day 7, Week 4, Month 3, and Month 6. Glucocorticoid (GC) dose was standardized to prednisone-equivalent mg/kg/day. Eight women (mean age 29.9 ± 12.8 years) were included, and anakinra was initiated at the time of MAS diagnosis in six patients, 2 months after MAS diagnosis in one and 2 months before MAS onset in one. Of the seven patients starting anakinra at or after MAS onset, all achieved Targets 1 and 2 and CID at a median of 1.5 months (range 1-5), and all maintained remission for ≥ 6 months; no severe adverse events were observed. Mean prednisone-equivalent dose fell from 1.63 ± 0.59 to 0.16 ± 0.09 mg/kg/day (p < 0.01). Four patients discontinued anakinra within 6 months for reasons of cost and access rather than disease flare. Add-on therapy with anakinra was associated with rapid achievement of EULAR/PReS targets, sustained remission, and substantial GC sparing in severe Still's disease-associated MAS.

items.title: Hydroxychloroquine therapy and its impact on bone mineral density among systemic lupus erythematosus patients: A cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) are at increased risk of osteoporosis due to chronic inflammation, prolonged glucocorticoid (GC) exposure, and treatment-related factors. Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ), a cornerstone of SLE therapy, has shown conflicting effects on bone health. This study examined the association between HCQ use and bone mineral density (BMD) in SLE. A cross-sectional study of 213 SLE patients was conducted at Dr. Soetomo General Academic Hospital. BMD was assessed by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) and classified using WHO criteria. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and treatment-related variables were collected. Group comparisons employed chi-square and non-parametric tests, while ordinal logistic regression identified independent predictors of reduced BMD. Among 213 patients, 22.5% had normal BMD, 51.2% osteopenia, and 26.3% osteoporosis. Independent predictors of reduced BMD were older age (OR 1.05, 95% CI 1.01-1.09), higher cumulative GC exposure (OR 1.07, 95% CI 1.02-1.12), and lower BMI (OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.80-0.98). Importantly, the use of HCQ has been linked to a protective effect against osteoporosis (OR 0.47, 95% CI 0.22-0.97, P = 0.040). Neither SLEDAI scores nor complement/ESR levels were significantly associated with BMD. Low BMD is highly prevalent in SLE and is strongly influenced by age, GC exposure, and BMI. HCQ use was linked to a protective effect on bone health, plausibly mediated by anti-resorptive, antioxidant, and glucocorticoid-sparing properties. Although a causal relationship between these two variables cannot yet be established, this association underscores the need for further well-designed longitudinal or interventional studies.

items.title: Development and Preliminary Psychometric Validation of the Gout Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices (G-KAP) Questionnaire: An Asia-Pacific Multicenter Study.
items.abstract: To develop and undertake preliminary psychometric validation of the Gout Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices (G-KAP) Questionnaire for patients with gout in multiple Asia-Pacific clinical settings. Six development experts and nine relevance experts reviewed the English 56-question instrument. Analyses included 312 baseline participants from 10 countries and 117 paired assessments; 149 participants formed an additional recruitment-wave subset. Language assistance involved oral explanation without a fixed translation script. We evaluated content relevance, keyed knowledge reliability, item-level stability, and exploratory structure using explicit coding and missing-data rules. S-CVI/Ave was 0.998 across 68 rated rows. The 19-indicator knowledge score averaged 56.1% ± 20.3%; KR-20 was 0.770 and common-factor omega 0.764. Absolute-agreement single-measure ICC was 0.763 (95% bootstrap CI 0.635-0.857); mean retest increase was 2.34 percentage points (p = 0.037). Numeric attitude ICCs ranged 0.345-0.838. Among 303 complete cases for 38 exploratory indicators, full-matrix and common-factor parallel analyses suggested 7 and 11 dimensions. The seven-factor comparison model included two weak two-item factors and ambiguous cross-loadings. The English G-KAP shows strong expert-rated relevance and encouraging preliminary knowledge-score reliability. Oral-assistance variability, unequal recruitment and uncertain dimensionality limit interpretation. Cross-cultural validity, measurement invariance, attitude/practice composite scores and clinical effectiveness are unestablished. Standardized administration, linguistic adaptation and independent confirmatory evaluation are needed before cross-country comparison or subscale development.

items.title: Screening of Active Ingredients From Ficus tikoua Bur. Against Rheumatoid Arthritis and Their Enrichment Using a β-Cyclodextrin-Based Monolith.
items.abstract: Ficus tikoua Bur., a perennial creeping woody liana belonging to the genus Ficus (Moraceae), has been traditionally used in combination therapies for rheumatoid arthritis (RA). This study aimed to screen active components from F. tikoua Bur. against RA. Prior to activity testing, compounds with appropriate polarity and size were enriched by a homemade β-cyclodextrin-based monolithic material when adjusting the polarity of the enrichment mobile phase. Anti-inflammatory activity evaluations of different fractions were conducted using Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) assay and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Results showed that the compounds in F. tikoua Bur. had no significant effect on RAW264.7 cell viability while effectively reducing secretion levels of inflammatory cytokines IL-6 and TNF-α. When a mixture of methanol and water (30:70, v/v) was used as the enrichment mobile phase, those components adsorbed on the monolith exhibited optimal inhibition effects on IL-6 and TNF-α production. Further separation and LC-MS analysis of the most active fraction, combined with literature data, 4-hydroxy-3,5-bis(3'-methyl-2-butenyl) benzoic acid-O-β-D-glucopyranoside may be the primary anti-inflammatory constituent. Optimization of enrichment conditions revealed that the monolithic material achieved an enrichment factor of 15.352 for the screened compound.

items.title: Autoimmune Conversion of Hashimoto's Thyroiditis to Graves' Disease With Immune Pancytopenia in a Patient With Seropositive Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Diagnostic and Therapeutic Conundrum.
items.abstract: Autoimmune conversion of Hashimoto's thyroiditis (HT) to Graves' disease (GD) is an uncommon phenomenon. The coexistence of GD, seropositive rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and pancytopenia presents a rare diagnostic and therapeutic challenge, particularly when antithyroid drug (ATD) therapy is contemplated in the presence of pre-existing cytopenias. A 66-year-old woman with a four-year history of hypothyroidism on levothyroxine replacement and long-standing seropositive RA presented with generalized weakness, altered bowel habits, and insomnia. Serial thyroid function tests (TFTs) had demonstrated progressive suppression of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), necessitating dose reduction and eventual discontinuation of levothyroxine. Evaluation revealed thyrotoxicosis with elevated free thyroxine (FT4), free triiodothyronine (FT3), raised antithyroid peroxidase and TSH receptor antibodies, diffuse goiter with increased vascularity on Doppler ultrasonography, and diffusely increased uptake on thyroid scintigraphy, confirming Graves' disease. Concurrent investigations demonstrated pancytopenia with elevated liver enzymes and mild splenomegaly. Given the presence of seropositive rheumatoid arthritis and the exclusion of alternative causes of pancytopenia, an immune-mediated mechanism leading to bone marrow suppression was suspected. After treatment with granulocyte colony-stimulating factor, carbimazole was cautiously initiated with close hematological monitoring. The patient showed progressive clinical and hematological improvement. This case highlights the rare transition from Hashimoto's thyroiditis to Graves' disease in a patient with seropositive RA and immune-mediated pancytopenia. It underscores the importance of considering autoimmune thyroid conversion in previously hypothyroid patients with persistent TSH suppression and demonstrates that carefully monitored antithyroid therapy can be safely administered despite pre-existing pancytopenia within a multidisciplinary care framework.

items.title: Early Manifestations of Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA), a rare autoimmune disease formerly known as Wegener's granulomatosis, is characterized by systemic necrotizing vasculitis that primarily affects small- to medium-sized vessels. Classically, GPA manifests in the respiratory tract and kidneys; however, its early symptoms can be nonspecific, complicating timely diagnosis. This report describes the case of a 43-year-old Caucasian male presenting with progressive polyarthralgia, intermittent fever, weight loss, and other systemic symptoms over three months. Initial clinical findings, including night sweats, fatigue, and a dry cough, were nonspecific and prompted further diagnostic investigations. His condition progressed with worsening anemia, declining kidney function, and elevated inflammatory markers. Diagnostic evaluation, including serologic testing and renal biopsy, ultimately confirmed the diagnosis of GPA with pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis. This report underscores the importance of comprehensive history-taking, thorough physical examination, and a systemic approach to clinical evaluation. It highlights the critical role of primary care physicians in recognizing subtle, systemic symptoms that may point to an underlying autoimmune disease and coordinating early referrals for appropriate diagnostic testing. Timely recognition of GPA can improve outcomes, particularly when appropriate treatment is initiated promptly.

items.title: Monoclonal Interstitial Nephritis with IgA-Kappa Plasma Cells Deposition in Sjögren Syndrome: A Case Report.
items.abstract: In Sjögren syndrome, tubulointerstitial involvement is a frequent finding, characterized by lymphoplasmacytic infiltration, tubular atrophy, and interstitial fibrosis. Nevertheless, descriptions of monoclonal interstitial infiltrates remain scarce. These observations suggest that beyond the classical spectrum of glomerular or tubular injury, a subset of patients with Sjögren syndrome may present atypical renal manifestations potentially associated with underlying monoclonal gammopathy of renal significance. This highlights the importance of accurately characterizing infiltrates and carefully considering monoclonal gammopathy of renal significance (MGRS) as a potential contributor to disease heterogeneity and long-term kidney outcomes. An 83-year-old woman with Sjögren syndrome presented with a rapidly progressive decline in kidney function, without proteinuria. Immunologic and viral workup was unremarkable. A kidney biopsy revealed marked interstitial plasma cell infiltration, as demonstrated by CD138+ staining and IgA-kappa restriction by immunohistochemistry, with no glomerular involvement. Bone marrow evaluation showed <10% plasma cells, excluding multiple myeloma. Serum electrophoresis confirmed an IgA-kappa monoclonal spike and abnormal free light chain ratio. Chemotherapy with bortezomib, dexamethasone, and lenalidomide resulted in an improvement of kidney function and normalization of IgA levels. The interstitium is frequently overlooked in MGRS classification; however, interstitial monoclonal plasma cell infiltration has recently been described in a subgroup of patients with Sjögren syndrome. It may represent a novel entity within MGRS, potentially enhancing prognosis through plasma cell-directed therapies.

items.title: Quality of Care of Patients with Gout in Primary Care Settings in the Philippines.
items.abstract: Despite established treatment guidelines, variations in the management of patients with gout in primary care settings are observed, leading to suboptimal patient outcomes. This study aimed to describe the quality of care among adult patients with gout who consulted in selected urban, rural, and remote primary care sites in the Philippines. This retrospective study involved review of electronic medical records (EMR) of adult patients diagnosed with gout between 2016 and 2022 in three primary care clinics in urban, rural, and remote settings in the Philippines. Quality of care was assessed based on adherence to predefined quality indicators from recommendations of the 2016 EULAR guidelines for gout management, including lifestyle counseling, comorbidity screening, prescription of recommended anti-inflammatory agents to patients with acute gout, and urate-lowering therapy (ULT) prescription. A total of 557 patients were included in the study. The cohort was predominantly male (67.1%), with a mean age of 55.2 years. Young-onset gout (age <40 years) was present in 18.1% of patients. The remote site had the lowest rate of baseline SUA determination at only 7.7%, with no patient having follow-up SUA determination. The mean baseline SUA level was 8.8 mg/dL, with the highest baseline SUA seen at the remote site (9.6 mg/dL). Screening rates for comorbidities were also suboptimal at 2.5%. Appropriate anti-inflammatory treatment for acute gouty flares was provided in 45.6% of patients, with the lowest adherence at the rural site (17.6%). The majority (90%) of the 20 patients who were identified to have indications for ULT were prescribed ULTs. Prescription of allopurinol as first-line ULT was highest in the rural (69.1%) and remote sites (65.9%) and lowest in the urban site (36.7%). Overutilization of ULT was observed across the 3 sites (36.1%), with the highest overutilization observed in the remote (52.1%) and rural sites (34.6%). Health disparities were observed, with the remote site having the highest overutilization of non-recommended analgesics, the least frequent serum uric acid determination, and the least frequent follow-up consults. Highest overutilization of ULT was observed in the urban and remote sites. The rural site had the highest percentage of patients with severe disease and the lowest adherence to the prescription of appropriate anti-inflammatory therapy for acute gouty arthritis and screening for comorbidities. These findings reflect the need to improve gout management in primary care and highlight the need for targeted strategies appropriate according to the setting, especially in underserved populations in rural and remote areas.

items.title: Prevalence of Psoriatic Arthritis among Patients with Psoriasis Using the Psoriatic Arthritis Screening Tool (PEST) Questionnaire in a Tertiary Government Institution.
items.abstract: Psoriatic arthritis (PsA) is a complex musculoskeletal disorder that is associated with psoriasis. Its estimated prevalence among patients with psoriasis ranges widely from 6% to 42% in Europe, North America, and South Africa. However, there is a paucity of data in Asia. To date, there is no local study done in the Philippines. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of psoriatic arthritis (PsA) among patients with psoriasis in a tertiary institution. This is a descriptive cross-sectional study that included 150 patients with psoriasis in the Dermatology Clinic. Demographic and clinical data were collected. Psoriatic Arthritis Screening Tool (PEST) was applied to all participants. Those who scored ≥3 on the PEST were seen at the Rheumatology Clinic and confirmed with the Classification of Psoriatic Arthritis (CASPAR) Criteria. Descriptive statistics were used to describe the demographic and clinical characteristics. The prevalence of psoriatic arthritis among patients with psoriasis was calculated as the percentage of the population who scored ≥3 on the CASPAR Criteria. Out of the 150 patients with psoriasis, a total of 50 scored ≥3 on PEST. Of these, 47 patients (31.3%) qualified for the diagnosis of PsA using the CASPAR criteria. Thirty-seven out of the forty-seven patients (79%) are known PsA patients, while the remaining 10 patients (21%) were newly diagnosed with PsA. A total of 34 patients (72%) were female, with a mean age of 33 and 39 years at the onset of psoriasis and PsA, respectively. Family history of psoriasis was present in 22 patients (47%). The most common pattern of arthritis was polyarticular (51%) followed by oligoarticular (38%) and axial (11%). Morning stiffness was present in 83% of the patients. Dactylitis was recorded in 16 patients (34%), while 19 patients (40%) had enthesopathy. Onycholysis was the most common nail abnormality seen in 20 patients (43%). Only 13 patients had rheumatoid factor at baseline, and all were negative. Most of the patients did not have imaging studies at baseline. In this single center study, the diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis among patients who were previously diagnosed with psoriasis increased from 24.5% to 31.3% using PEST as a screening tool, showing its usefulness in improving clinical detection of psoriatic arthritis among these patients.

items.title: Anti-Transcriptional Intermediary Factor 1 Gamma Antibody-Positive Dermatomyositis Concomitant with Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma: Case Report and Literature Review.
items.abstract: Anti-transcriptional intermediary factor 1 gamma antibody-positive dermatomyositis (anti-TIF1-γ-DM) is a paraneoplastic syndrome occurring in various neoplasms, but reports elaborating on anti-TIF1-γ-DM patients accompanied by lymphoma are scarce. We report 2 patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) complicated by anti-TIF1-γ-DM and carried out TIF1-γ immunohistochemistry on tissue sections of DLBCL and skin of anti-TIF1-γ-DM patients and controls. Genetic analysis of exons 2 and 10 of TRIM33 , the gene coding TIF1-γ, was also carried out in DLBCL and skin samples of anti-TIF1-γ-DM patients and controls to look for recurrent mutations. Case 1 was a 65-year-old male and case 2 was a 52-year-old male, and both patients presented with DLBCL complicated by anti-TIF1-γ-DM. R-CHOP (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, prednisolone) therapy led to remissions of both anti-TIF1-γ-DM and DLBCL in both cases. Immunohistochemistry showed strong TIF1-γ expression in DLBCL and skin samples from both patients with anti-TIF1-γ-DM and controls. Mutations in exons 2 and 10 of TRIM33 have been previously reported in DLBCL cells of an anti-TIF1-γ-DM patient, but analysis of the same exons revealed no recurrent mutations in our cases. Anti-TIF1-γ-DM very often presents with a concomitant neoplasm, and a systemic evaluation for malignancy including lymphoma is mandatory. The etiology of anti-TIF1-γ-DM in patients with lymphoma remains unknown, and the underlying mechanisms have yet to be elucidated.

items.title: Bilateral Foot Drop as the Presenting Manifestation of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus-Associated Mononeuritis Multiplex: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Peripheral nervous system involvement in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is uncommon, and mononeuritis multiplex as the presenting neurological manifestation is particularly rare. Early recognition may be difficult when the initial clinical picture resembles focal compressive neuropathy. A 31-year-old previously healthy woman developed acute right foot numbness and foot drop after right knee pain and earlier nonspecific arthralgia. Initial assessments favored peroneal neurapraxia. Over the following 3 weeks, her deficits progressed to persistent right foot drop followed by new left lower limb numbness and weakness, resulting in asymmetric bilateral foot drop. Electrophysiological studies demonstrated an asymmetric, non-length-dependent motor and sensory axonal neuropathy consistent with mononeuritis multiplex. Magnetic resonance imaging of the lumbosacral spine excluded a compressive lumbosacral explanation and focused ultrasound showed no compressive lesion involving the right common peroneal nerve. Serological evaluation revealed high-titer antinuclear antibody, positive anti-double-stranded DNA, anti-Ro, anti-ribosomal P antibodies, elevated inflammatory markers, and a positive lupus anticoagulant screen, with negative infectious screening and no evidence of active lupus nephritis. She was treated with intravenous methylprednisolone, intravenous immunoglobulin, hydroxychloroquine, and rituximab, followed by oral corticosteroid tapering and rehabilitation. Her pain improved early, distal motor function partially recovered, and she later demonstrated meaningful functional improvement with orthotic and rehabilitation support. This case suggests that SLE may initially present predominantly as mononeuritis multiplex, with evolving bilateral foot drop as the dominant neurological and function-threatening manifestation, through a suspected vasculitic mechanism, even when more typical renal, serosal, or major mucocutaneous features are absent at neurological presentation. In patients with progressive or sequential foot drop, especially when the presentation becomes bilateral or multifocal, prompt electrodiagnostic testing and evaluation for systemic autoimmune disease are essential to avoid diagnostic delay and allow timely immunotherapy. Foot drop means difficulty lifting the front part of the foot, which can cause tripping or an abnormal walking pattern. It is often caused by pressure on a nerve near the knee or by a problem in the lower back. This case describes a 31-year-old woman who first developed numbness and weakness in her right foot. At first, her symptoms looked similar to a common nerve compression problem. Over the next few weeks, she developed symptoms in both legs. Nerve tests showed that several separate nerves were affected. This pattern is called mononeuritis multiplex. Blood tests also supported a new diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus, an autoimmune disease in which the immune system can attack the body’s own tissues. In this patient, the nerve problem was considered most likely related to lupus-associated inflammation of the small blood vessels that supply the nerves, although this was not confirmed by nerve biopsy. She was treated with medicines to reduce immune system activity, including steroids, intravenous immunoglobulin, hydroxychloroquine, and rituximab. She also received physiotherapy and ankle-foot supports to improve walking. Her pain and movement improved, although some weakness remained during follow-up. This case highlights that worsening or bilateral foot drop should not always be assumed to be due to simple nerve compression. When symptoms progress or affect both sides, doctors should consider inflammatory and autoimmune causes and arrange appropriate nerve and blood tests.

items.title: Drug interactions in rheumatoid arthritis: a disparity between electronic database prediction and real-world co-prescription with different large language models.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic inflammatory disease that often requires multi-drug regimens, which can increase the risk of drug-drug interactions (DDIs). To determine whether polypharmacy contributes to potential DDIs in patients with RA. A retrospective observational study that integrates data from drug interaction databases and medical records, supplemented by artificial intelligence analysis. Twenty-one RA drugs and 54 commonly prescribed medicines were screened for potential DDIs using the Micromedex and WebMD databases and compared with real-world co-prescription at our hospital. The ChatGPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 large language models (LLMs) were also evaluated as "AI judges" versus an expert rheumatologist to assess real-world co-prescription. This study was conducted from January to September 2025. Among 75 frequently prescribed medicines in RA patients, 753 database-predicted potential DDIs were reported, with Micromedex showing 464 DDI pairs and WebMD showing 600 pairs. Both databases classified 47 serious potential DDIs as contraindicated or major, with high concordance. The main predicted DDI mechanisms were immunosuppression (27%), methotrexate toxicity (18%), and nephrotoxicity (12%), with tacrolimus (12%), methotrexate (10%), and infliximab (6%) as major culprit drugs. In real-world co-prescriptions, 259 RA patients showed methotrexate/naproxen (46.4%) and methotrexate/sulfasalazine (29.5%) as the most common real-world co-prescribing patterns with potential DDIs. Brennan-Prediger kappa values indicated fair agreement (0.3161) in the electronic database predictions and conditional agreement (0.9807) among preselected serious DDIs. The LLM evaluation revealed that advanced models (e.g., Gemini 2.5 Pro) provided finesse recommendations highly concordant with expert opinion, whereas simpler models were more conservatively aligned with database alerts. In both real-world co-prescription and database evaluation, serious potential DDIs were associated mainly with methotrexate toxicity. Based on these exploratory findings, advanced LLMs show potential to assist with the contextualizing rigid database alerts and supporting pragmatic clinical decision-making. However, expert clinical judgment and direct patient consultation remain essential to improve RA patient safety and medication adherence. Comparative drug interactions in rheumatoid arthritis patients Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a complex disease that requires multiple medications and might cause drug-drug interactions (DDIs). There is inadequate information comparing potential DDI predictions between electronic database and real-world co-prescription, especially with AI support. Our study revealed a high number of potential DDIs among medicines commonly prescribed for RA patients. Furthermore, the significant discordance in DDI predictions was detected between the electronic database and the real-world co-prescription, with large language models (LLMs). The real-world co-prescription indicated that methotrexate and NSAIDs/sulfasalazine pose a high risk for serious DDIs. By using advanced LLMs provided nuanced advice consistent with expert rheumatologist consensus by continuing treatment with careful monitoring for these serious DDIs. Management of harmful DDIs requires integrating modern decision support tools, deep clinical expertise, and direct patient communication.

items.title: Current aspects of the etiopathogenesis of antiphospholipid syndrome and its clinical manifestations.
items.abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome is a systemic autoimmune disorder characterized by the persistent presence of antiphospholipid antibodies and a predisposition to arterial, venous, and microvascular thrombotic manifestations. In this article, the authors analyzed the available literature sources in the PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar databases for the period from 2019 to 2026, focusing on the epidemiological, gender-related, etiopathogenetic, clinical, and diagnostic aspects of antiphospholipid syndrome. Antiphospholipid syndrome emerges as a systemic immune-vascular nosological entity in which cerebrovascular and cardiovascular manifestations constitute the main clinical phenotype and determine the long-term prognosis of the disease. Understanding antiphospholipid syndrome as a unified immune-coagulation process is of fundamental importance for clinical practice, as it provides a basis for more accurate risk stratification, early identification of patients with a high probability of severe vascular complications, and the development of pathogenetically substantiated therapeutic methods targeting not only the coagulation cascade but also the immune and inflammatory components of the disease. Such an integrative approach is fundamental to optimizing treatment and improving the prognosis of patients with antiphospholipid syndrome.

items.title: Expression Profile of the IL-17 Receptor Family on Peripheral B Lymphocytes in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: B cells are key contributors to the immunopathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), yet the expression profile of interleukin-17 (IL-17) receptors on human B cells remains incompletely defined. We analyzed the surface expression of IL-17RA-IL-17RE on peripheral CD19 + B cells from 42 patients with RA and 20 healthy controls (HC) using flow cytometry. Receptor-positive cell frequency and mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) were evaluated, and disease activity was assessed using the Disease Activity Score in 28 joints based on erythrocyte sedimentation rate (DAS28-ESR). The frequency of receptor-positive B cells differed significantly among IL-17 receptor (IL-17R) family members in both RA and HC, with IL-17RD showing the highest proportion of positive cells, followed by IL-17RA, whereas IL-17RC was less frequent and IL-17RB and IL-17RE were rarely detected. The proportion of IL-17RA + B cells was lower in RA than in HC and remained statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons (Holm-adjusted p = 0.0126). A nominally lower frequency of IL-17RC + B cells in RA did not remain significant after adjustment, while IL-17RD frequency was comparable between groups. No between-group differences in MFI remained significant after multiple-comparison correction. Receptor expression was not significantly associated with DAS28-ESR disease activity categories. These findings provide a descriptive characterization of the IL-17R family on peripheral B cells in RA and identify a lower frequency of IL-17RA + B cells as the most robust between-group difference, suggesting alterations in IL-17R dynamics that may contribute to B-cell dysregulation and disease pathogenesis.

items.title: A Multidisciplinary Neuro-Lupus Program for the Evaluation and Management of Patients With SLE and Cognitive Concerns.
items.abstract: To develop and implement a standardized, comprehensive multidisciplinary program for the evaluation and management of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and cognitive concerns that would lead to improved diagnosis and management. The Neuro-Lupus Program evaluated 50 patients with SLE referred for any neurocognitive concern over a 12-month period. A specific sequential work-up protocol was developed for standardized patient evaluation. Initial history and examination were performed by a dedicated lupus neurologist followed by referral for comprehensive neurocognitive testing. Patients with suspected mood or psychotic disorders were evaluated in a specialized autoimmune psychiatry clinic. MRI brain scans were performed in all patients. Patients with MRI evidence of inflammation or cognitive impairment were further assessed with CSF studies and FDG-PET/CT brain. Management of neuropsychiatric medications and immunotherapy was a collaboration between neurology, psychiatry, and rheumatology. Full neurocognitive evaluation revealed a previously undiagnosed cognitive impairment in 46.4% of patients tested (mild 39.3%, major 7.1%), with an additional 39.3% demonstrating a normal cognitive profile with isolated weakness. MRI demonstrated white matter disease in 50% of patients and cerebral atrophy in 10%. Brain FDG-PET/CT was performed in 8 patients (16%), 7 (88%) of which were abnormal. CSF studies demonstrated normal protein and white cell counts, but 25% had elevated kappa free light chains. As a result of this program, neuropsychiatric medications were optimized in 86% of patients and 8% had an escalation in immunotherapy. This multidisciplinary Neuro-Lupus Program model brings together neurologists, psychiatrists, rheumatologists, and neuropsychologists to standardize the approach to neurocognitive symptoms in SLE. Among the patients enrolled, this program detected previously undiagnosed cognitive impairment in the majority of those tested and was associated with changes in neuropsychiatric and immunotherapy management.
